title: Nullish coalescing and optional chaining
learningObjectives: Explain nullish coalescing and optional chaining and write clear, safe expressions.

understand.concept: The nullish coalescing operator ?? uses its right-hand value only when the left-hand value is null or undefined. Optional chaining ?. safely accesses a property, method, or index when the value before it is nullish, returning undefined instead of throwing.
understand.whyItMatters: These operators help handle optional data without treating valid falsy values such as 0 or an empty string as missing. They do not replace validation of data shape or authorization.
understand.analogy: ?? asks whether a value is absent; optional chaining checks whether the next step is safe to access.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; operator evaluation and coercion follow JavaScript precedence and conversion rules.

explain.narrative: The name is Asha and the limit remains 0 because zero is not nullish.

examples.explanation: The name is Asha and the limit remains 0 because zero is not nullish.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console or page displays the expression results described.

practise.guidedTask: Create a nested object with a missing optional property. Use optional chaining and ?? while preserving valid zero and empty-string values.
practise.independentTask: Write a small program that uses the operator or numeric rule in a practical example. Predict results, run the code, and explain any coercion.
hints: Preserve valid falsy values when using defaults.
Validate numeric inputs and check finite results.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Nullish coalescing and optional chaining</title></head><body>
<script>const settings={profile:{name:'Asha'},limit:0};const name=settings.profile?.name??'Guest';const limit=settings.limit??10;console.log(name,limit);</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: What values trigger the fallback in the nullish coalescing operator?
questions.explanation: ?? uses the fallback only when the left operand is null or undefined.

questions.prompt: What should you do before using a value in a numeric calculation?
options: Assume it is already a valid number
questions.explanation: Explicit conversion and validation prevent invalid or imprecise values from entering calculations.
